body: According to [this](http://eslint.org/blog/2016/02/eslint-v2.0.0-released#shareable-config-changes), it should pick up dependencies in the shareable config package.

Hi @jsonmaur, thanks for the issue. It looks like there's not enough information for us to know how to help you. If you're reporting a bug, please be sure to include:
1. The version of ESLint you are using (run `eslint -v`)
2. What you did (the source code and ESLint configuration)
3. The actual ESLint output complete with numbers
4. What you expected to happen instead

Requesting a new rule? Please see [Proposing a New Rule](http://eslint.org/docs/developer-guide/contributing/new-rules) for instructions.

If it's something else, please just provide as much additional information as possible. Thanks!

@jsonmaur I'm not quite sure if you're reporting a bug or asking a question here. Since you are talking about unexpected behavior/being unable to do something, could you please answer the questions [here](https://github.com/eslint/eslint/issues/5411#issuecomment-189681270)? Then we'll be able to more easily determine if we have a bug here. Thanks!

Sorry I wasn't more clear--I'm reporting a bug. I'm not able to extend a shareable config from another shareable config, unless I'm running Node >= 5. So if I'm running Node 4.3 for example and I run `npm install --save-dev eslint eslint-config-google` in a new project (which extends from `eslint-config-xo`), it throws this error:

```
/Users/jsonmaur/Desktop/eslint-test/node_modules/eslint/lib/config/config-file.js:361
            throw e;
            ^

Error: Cannot find module 'eslint-config-xo' from '/Users/jsonmaur/Desktop/eslint-test/node_modules'
Referenced from: google
Referenced from: /Users/jsonmaur/Desktop/eslint-test/.eslintrc
    at Function.module.exports [as sync] (/Users/jsonmaur/Desktop/eslint-test/node_modules/eslint/node_modules/resolve/lib/sync.js:33:11)
    at resolve (/Users/jsonmaur/Desktop/eslint-test/node_modules/eslint/lib/config/config-file.js:417:38)
    at load (/Users/jsonmaur/Desktop/eslint-test/node_modules/eslint/lib/config/config-file.js:436:24)
    at /Users/jsonmaur/Desktop/eslint-test/node_modules/eslint/lib/config/config-file.js:355:36
    at Array.reduceRight (native)
    at applyExtends (/Users/jsonmaur/Desktop/eslint-test/node_modules/eslint/lib/config/config-file.js:338:28)
    at load (/Users/jsonmaur/Desktop/eslint-test/node_modules/eslint/lib/config/config-file.js:464:22)
    at /Users/jsonmaur/Desktop/eslint-test/node_modules/eslint/lib/config/config-file.js:355:36
    at Array.reduceRight (native)
    at applyExtends (/Users/jsonmaur/Desktop/eslint-test/node_modules/eslint/lib/config/config-file.js:338:28)
```

So although the `eslint-config-xo` dependency is installed as part of `eslint-config-google`, eslint doesn't seem to pick it up. This is running eslint 2.2.0 in Node 4.3.1. If I use Node 5.7 and reinstall the npm dependencies, things work as expected.
It seems to be a problem with npm versions earlier than 3.0, rather than the Node version. Probably because of the deduplicated dependencies.
Is there anything ESLint could/should do to work around the npm version issue? At this point, it doesn't sound like there's anything we can do here, but I'm not an npm expert by any means.

Nor am I. But I would assume ESLint should resolve the dependency the same way Node resolves modules. First looking in the project dependencies to work with npm@3, then looking in the shareable config dependencies to work for npm@2 if the former doesn't exist, then throwing an error if neither exist. I'm not familiar with eslint's core, otherwise I'd take a shot at a PR. If I get some time this week I'll see if I can come up with something.

Sounds like a bug.

As far as I know, ESLint has been resolving `extends` property relatively from the config file since #5023.

Yeah, this is a bug. It looks like we are resolving from too high up the directory tree. 

@jsonmaur can you share your directory structure? Specifically, I'd like to see where eslint-config-google and eslint-config-xo are installed relative to your project.
@nzakas He shared a test repo in the [original issue](https://github.com/google/eslint-config-google/issues/8): https://github.com/jsonmaur/eslint-test

Thanks @sindresorhus. @nzakas If using npm@3, it will dedupe dependencies, so eslint-config-google and eslint-config-xo will be in the project dependencies. But if using npm@2, eslint-config-xo will be under the dependencies of eslint-config-google.
